public_rationale: There were credible reports of difficulties beyond OpenAI. That supports the narrower statement that several labs faced disappointing results. It does not establish the claimed field-wide decline in returns from scaling. Company disagreement and DeepSeek's technical progress also prevent treating the reports as conclusive. These competing signals do not establish a mixed outcome because they do not measure the same scaling relationship.
limitations: Reporting is used because comparable primary measurements were not found.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Diminishing returns from scaling affect the whole AI field, not just OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: It’s not just OpenAI either; it’s the whole field, as I discussed in my own recent Fortune article:

from_speaker: scaling just isn’t producing the fruit that it once did
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that additional pretraining scale was producing smaller capability gains across major frontier developers.
The surrounding discussion concerns frontier generative models, rather than every application of AI.
I interpret 'whole field' as a widespread industry trend, not a claim that every laboratory experienced identical results.
The comparison concerns the current frontier-model development cycle, operationalized as November 2024 through publication. This reporting window is evaluator-supplied.
Disappointing expectations or delayed releases alone do not establish declining returns per unit of scale.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable results or well-substantiated reporting establish that additional pretraining scale yielded smaller capability gains across several major developers than in their preceding model generations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence across major developers establishes that returns to additional pretraining scale remained broadly comparable to, or exceeded, those of preceding generations.

evidence.excerpt: leading AI companies are experiencing diminishing returns
evidence.explanation: This corroborates that slowdown reports extended beyond OpenAI. The same article records Anthropic's disagreement and uncertainty about whether high expectations explain the reported disappointments; it supplies no comparable scaling curves.

evidence.excerpt: performance comparable to leading closed-source models
evidence.explanation: The report documents substantial contemporary progress outside the named US labs. It combines architectural and training changes, so it neither isolates pretraining scale nor establishes whether its marginal returns had declined.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable training-resource and capability results for successive generations at several major labs, or sufficiently detailed independent reporting of those experiments.
